solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: in tells us the detectives are placed inside the word for action

parts.note: an action or act is a deed
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police detectives in the middle of an operation are sure of their case.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain and decided are synonyms, both describing something settled beyond doubt.

indicators.note: broken signals the letters of the two words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A houseplant dies because its pot cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like greenery; it is the verb, as in planting evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant something is to deposit or place it, as one puts down a load.

clue.text: Fellow tenor with Queen on stage

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A tenor and a queen share the stage in an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on stage' reads as performing; on is a link and stage is the definition, a phase of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapter is a stage or phase, as in a new chapter in one's life.

clue.text: Starts to dole out sedative, easing sickness

definitions.text: Starts to dole out sedative, easing sickness

indicators.note: starts to means take the beginning of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A nurse begins to give out a sedative to ease illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as building it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doses are measured amounts of medicine, like the sedative given out to ease illness.

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
to miss a chance is to lose it
Al Capone, the famous Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Police lose track of a gangster who gets shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting bullet' suggests a shooting; 'the bullet' is British slang for being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the bullet is informal for being fired, so bullet means dismissal.

clue.text: Covering up for Roman Catholic clergy?

definitions.text: Covering up for Roman Catholic clergy?

parts.words: Covering up for Roman Catholic clergy
parts.note: reads like a church cover-up scandal, but means a covering worn on top of the head by Catholic priests

explanation.surface: A hint at the Church concealing its priests' misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering up' suggests concealment; read it as a covering worn up on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The biretta is the square ridged cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy, a head covering.

clue.text: Black look giving French stick, perhaps

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to read is to look at and understand

explanation.surface: A dark glance gives a French person a beating, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French stick' is a baguette, a long loaf; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A French stick, or baguette, is one example of a loaf.

clue.text: Tries again with a learner for practice

parts.note: a court that rehears a case tries it again
L is for learner, from British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A learner keeps making attempts until it becomes practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run of a performance.

parts.note: seems to be a big-stakes gambler, but describes a huge wave rolling in

explanation.surface: A big-spending gambler.
explanation.walkthrough: A high roller is a lavish gambler; here it is literally a tall wave that rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an enormous sea wave caused by an earthquake, a very high roller.

clue.text: From the start, is a novice mechanic

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A beginner tradesman is described as being one right from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanic is an old term for a manual worker or skilled craftsman.

clue.text: Party leader steps up producing cheers

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Party

parts.note: to step something up is to raise it

explanation.surface: A political leader increases the pace, and the crowd applauds.
explanation.definitionFit: Praises is a verb synonym of cheers, both meaning to applaud or acclaim.

definitions.meaning: in British slang to fag is to tire out, as in 'fagged out'
the smoke and fumes an engine emits through its tailpipe

explanation.surface: A cigarette's smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: Fag (British slang for a cigarette) and smoke look like one picture; instead fag is the verb to tire, and smoke is engine fumes, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust is to tire out, and exhaust is also the fumes discharged by an engine.

clue.text: As I fed, it's becoming full

indicators.note: becoming signals that the words before change into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A diner remarks that after eating they are now replete.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfied can mean having eaten enough, so full in the sense of sated.

indicators.note: in places the mother's word inside the word for when

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
mum is MA, and the possessive gives MA'S

explanation.surface: The family gathers round when mother is at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or collect together a quantity of something.

indicators.note: taking means the answer is taken from within the run of words that follows on from cardiopath

explanation.surface: A heart patient in a hospital gown has his pulse measured.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a single beat or pulsation, like that of the heart.

indicators.note: outside says the word for behind goes round the letter for left

parts.note: the behind is the backside, the buttocks

explanation.surface: A footballer playing outside left slips behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside left' looks like a football wing position; outside is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to relapse into old bad habits, to slip back.

indicators.note: in puts the church abbreviation inside the word for a conclave

parts.note: a conclave is a private meeting, a session
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church split emerges from a meeting of cardinals.
explanation.definitionFit: Secession is a formal breaking away, so a schism or split from a body.

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the fish

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
to go into a room is to enter it

explanation.surface: Having had fish, someone heads into a fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chippy' looks like a British fish-and-chip shop, but it is also British slang for a carpenter, a woodworker.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is British slang for a woodworker, from the wood chips they make.

parts.note: seems to describe a sight defect, but means relating to seeing with two eyes at once

explanation.surface: Something to do with seeing two of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double vision' suggests blurred sight; it means vision using both eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Binocular describes sight using both eyes together, as with field glasses.

definitions.meaning: used as a mild curse in place of a stronger word

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone's remarkable good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damned lucky!' reads as one exclamation; the opposite-sounding word works as a polite substitute for damned.
explanation.definitionFit: Blessed means fortunate, and is also a euphemistic intensifier like damned.

parts.note: zero can mean no, as in no faults at all
vices are faults or failings

explanation.surface: Pupils who have nothing wrong with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Novices are beginners learning a trade or subject, students in a broad sense.

clue.text: Initially loath, one gathers it's common sense

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: One grudgingly concludes that something is only common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common sense' looks like the definition; common is the last of the five words whose first letters are taken, leaving sense alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic means sound reasoning, which is sense as in 'there is sense in that'.

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Is French style the height of cool?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gallic fashion' suggests French style; fashion is the verb to shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Glacial means icy, so extremely cold in temperature or manner.

parts.note: a cot is a small or camp bed
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a camp bed by a lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camp bed' looks like one item; camp alone is the definition, a faction.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a group sharing views, as is a coterie, a close circle.

clue.text: He lives, bizarrely, for some people

definitions.text: He lives, bizarrely, for some people

indicators.note: bizarrely says the letters of lives are arranged in a strange new way

explanation.surface: Some people bizarrely insist that a dead star is still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: some fans claim the King of rock and roll is still alive, and his name rearranges the word lives.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer famously died in 1977, yet some people claim sightings of him alive.

definitions.meaning: tart means sharp or acerbic in tone

explanation.surface: A slice of pastry being cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting tart looks like slicing a pastry; both words are adjectives meaning sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means vigorously incisive, both cutting and sharp in expression.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up and down means the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A view from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held, a view.

clue.text: Knaves with Queen in poker, for example

indicators.note: in puts the queen's letter inside the word for knaves

parts.note: cads are knaves, dishonourable men
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Jacks and a queen held in a poker hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Knaves and Queen look like playing cards in a poker hand; poker is the game being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a game of cards, so cards in the sense of card games generally.

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild or fanciful, so the letters of notices are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wonderful reviews for an actor's role.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a portion or part of a whole.

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the word for blunder goes inside

parts.note: a tier is a bank or row, as of seats
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A dog-like financial institution owns up to a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed of dog, and hound is used loosely for any dog.

parts.note: de is French for of
eau de cologne is a scent

explanation.surface: A drop of French perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a fall or drop downward.

clue.text: Break down and do the crossword again!

definitions.meaning: to ... a thing is to break it down into its parts
read as ..., to work out the puzzle a second time

explanation.surface: A frustrated solver gives up, then starts the puzzle over.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer as RE- plus solve.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve is to analyse into components, and re-solve is to solve again.
